narrative.overview:
The site is a Mac desktop. The desktop metaphor is structural, not a skin. Each section is an AppKit document window with a unified title bar, traffic lights and an opaque body, and on a mouse-driven screen of 1024px or wider it can be dragged by its title bar. The Dock at the bottom is the navigation, the solid menu bar at the top is the persistent header, Control Center (opened from its menu bar glyph) holds the visitor's settings, Spotlight (⌘K) is search, Quick Look is project detail, and a notification banner is the toast. Every new surface should answer one question first: which piece of macOS would do this job? Then draw that piece.

The world follows the visitor's appearance, as macOS does. Every UI colour is a CSS variable with a light value on `:root` and a dark value on `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and Control Center offers Light, Dark and Auto (Auto is the default and follows `prefers-color-scheme`). The default wallpaper is the Golden Gate photograph. Its light and dark versions crossfade over 600ms when the appearance changes. The Kildare hills SVG is the alternative wallpaper, with a night overlay in dark appearance. Visitors can also dim the wallpaper by up to 60% with a black overlay. The wallpaper carries the atmosphere and is the only large saturated field on the page.

The desktop runs at the density of macOS itself. Controls are small (13px text, 28 to 36px targets on fine pointers, 44px on coarse), grey chrome is quiet, and a few large system-face headlines carry the content weight. There is one interface accent, system blue, and it does the jobs it does in AppKit: default buttons, selected rows, switches that are on, focus rings and links. Finder tag dots are the only other hues, and they label groups. There is no liquid glass and no backdrop blur: floating chrome uses the near-opaque vibrant material so animation stays at 60fps. Confirmed rejections from the product thesis: no dark hero band, no giant-name hero, no card grid of projects.
keyCharacteristics: Two appearances from one token set: light and dark values for every UI colour, switched on `<html data-theme>` with a 350ms colour ease.
Sections are windows: 12px corners, a 48px chrome title bar with traffic lights, an opaque body, and a three-layer window shadow. Windows can be dragged by the title bar from 1024px.
Navigation is macOS furniture: a solid menu bar, a vibrant Dock with a running-indicator dot, Spotlight, and Control Center.
System blue is the only accent. Finder tag colours appear only as small dots.
One floating material: `vibrant`, near-opaque with no backdrop filter.
The system face: SF Pro on Apple devices, with Geist as the fallback elsewhere. Headlines use tight negative tracking, and 13px is the control size.
Motion is spring-based and brief. Every animation collapses under `prefers-reduced-motion` and under Control Center's Focus switch.

rules.name: The Token Or Nothing Rule
rules.body: Every UI colour goes through a CSS variable that has both a light and a dark value. A literal hex on a surface is a bug in one of the two appearances.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: System blue is the only interface colour. If something needs to look pressable, selected, on or focused, it turns blue. If not, it stays grey.

rules.name: The Tag Dot Rule
rules.body: Finder tag colours label groups and do nothing else. They show up as dots of 10px or smaller, or as folder badges. They never fill buttons, text, backgrounds or headings.

rules.name: The Wallpaper Owns Colour Rule
rules.body: Big saturated areas belong to the wallpaper. Windows, bars and panels stay neutral or vibrant.

rules.name: The System Size Rule
rules.body: Chrome speaks at 13px. Anything that is part of the desktop (menu, sidebar, list, title bar, field, Control Center tile) sits between 11 and 13px. Only content inside a window grows beyond 13.5px.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Group headers are small, semibold and in sentence case, as in the Finder sidebar and Control Center. Numbers in lists, clocks, counts and money use tabular figures.

rules.name: The Hold My Code Exception
rules.body: The Hold My Code panel copies the shipped app 2.5.1, so it uses the app's own compact type: 10.5px uppercase labels at 0.04em tracking, and 10.5 to 11px captions. This type lives only inside that panel.

rules.name: The Hairline Edge Rule
rules.body: Opaque and vibrant surfaces are edged by a 0.5px ring inside the shadow stack, never by a 1px CSS border. Real borders are only for internal dividers (`rule`).

rules.name: The Focus Stack Rule
rules.body: Only one window reads as focused at a time. It gets coloured traffic lights and the full window shadow. Any window stacked behind it goes inactive. A dragged window rises to the top of the stack.

dos: **Do** put every new section in a Window with traffic lights, a 13px semibold title and a 12px corner radius. Choose the macOS app that would do the job (Finder, Mail, Quick Look, Preview) and draw its chrome.
**Do** take every UI colour from a CSS variable that has both a light and a dark value, and check the surface in both appearances.
**Do** keep System Blue (`accent`, `select`) for default buttons, selection, on-states, focus and links only.
**Do** use the vibrant material with the Menu shadow for small chrome floating over the wallpaper. Don't add backdrop-filter or blur animations.
**Do** edge opaque and vibrant surfaces with a 0.5px ring inside the shadow.

**Do** set type from the recorded ramp (11, 11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 14.5, 15, 17, 22px and the clamp display sizes), keep chrome text at 11 to 13px, group headers in sentence case, and figures tabular.
**Do** open detail in Quick Look or a sheet, and keep the page itself to one-line rows.
**Do** use springs for opening surfaces and 120ms ease for control states, and honour both `prefers-reduced-motion` and the Focus switch.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second interface accent. Finder tag colours stay as dots of 10px or smaller and as folder badges.
**Don't** hardcode a light-only colour (a white background, a black hairline, an `rgba(248,…)` panel) on a surface that has to work in dark appearance.
**Don't** put a dark hero band on the page. Dark appearance darkens the whole desktop at once, and no section is dark on its own.
**Don't** lay projects out as a grid of cards. Projects are rows in the Finder list.
**Don't** use 1px CSS borders as the outer edge of an opaque or vibrant floating surface. Use the 0.5px ring.
**Don't** fill large areas with saturated colour inside windows or bars. That field belongs to the wallpaper.

**Don't** use uppercase letter-spaced labels as section or group headers on new surfaces. The group-label pattern is sentence case. The only exception is the Hold My Code panel, because it copies the shipped app's UI.
**Don't** add type sizes below 11px outside the Hold My Code panel.
